proposed.justification: Strict improvement of the fixed-Bonferroni SOCP must remain decidable and independently checkable on degenerate cone faces. The in-house affine facial-reduction alternative proves that every reduction step has a multiplier of the required form; relative-interior strong duality then yields the attained facial dual used by the finite certificate. The construction and verifier terminate without any quantitative runtime claim.
proposed.consumer: An implementer or auditor can verify \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\) from finite rational design inputs even when the original conic program lacks ordinary Slater feasibility. The certificate concerns the fixed-Bonferroni SOCP surrogate; it does not alone certify strict improvement of the exact honest-width frontier \(W_s\), and it gives no runtime guarantee for \texttt{scpi} or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth}.

prose_updates.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking not-yet-treated donor sets. Conditional on the declared nonempty rational fixed design, this note maps every treated-unit--horizon error into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector and defines the jointly attainable bias set generated by the shared calendar-time coefficients and cellwise remainder bounds. The exact honest deterministic linear-band frontier is the attained minimum, over the relevant product of donor simplexes, of the worst shifted Gaussian-cube radius over that joint bias set. A fixed-Bonferroni bias-plus-standard-error SOCP remains finite-sample honest and within the stated dimension-uniform spectral factor of this exact frontier. A legal common-donor family with rational covariance factor proves that the square-root covariance-condition-number dependence is order-sharp for fixed Bonferroni calibration. Zero-bias Loewner and diagonal row-disjoint results give computable strict nested-width gains. Separately, an in-house affine facial-reduction alternative and relative-interior strong duality yield an exact finite primal--facial-dual certificate for strict SOCP improvement on degenerate faces, together with a terminating real-algebraic construction and verifier; no quantitative runtime bound is claimed. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein provide donor geometry only; \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are implementation consumers, not estimators covered by these theorems.

project_justification.fill: The note derives the deduplicated Gaussian contrast law and exact coordinate bias support function, proves finite-sample SOCP coverage, and characterizes the full bounded-mean frontier as an attained minimum over weights of a maximum shifted Gaussian-cube radius over the joint attainable bias set. It proves the spectral comparison and constructs a legal common-donor sequence on which the SOCP-to-exact-width ratio grows as the square root of the covariance condition number. Separate zero-bias Loewner, independent-coordinate product-root, and rational-witness results identify strict exact-frontier gains. For the general degenerate SOCP comparison, an in-house separation argument produces affine exposing multipliers at every facial-reduction step, after which relative-interior strong duality and effective real algebraic methods give a finite strict-gap certificate and a terminating verifier.

prose_updates.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2) supply the shrinking not-yet-treated donor-set geometry and note that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors even though their exposition and application focus on a common deepest pool. They do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide staggered prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; they do not give the joint attainable-bias min--max frontier or the order-sharp SOCP-to-frontier ratio proved here. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class. Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supplies the weak moving-set inequality used by the separate strict zero-bias Loewner result. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Pataki (2013) supplies the minimal-face, relative-Slater, strong-duality, and dual-attainment substrate used after reduction; the stronger affine-multiplier facial-reduction alternative needed by this certificate is proved in-house. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006, Theorems 13.11 and 14.16) support terminating real-closed-field quantifier elimination and sign-condition sampling with the stated sample-representation bounds; the note does not attribute a bit-complexity bound for the complete certificate construction to those excerpts. The present results retain the declared known-covariance experiment; they do not claim a covariance-estimation or published-class transfer theorem. \texttt{scpi} and \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are potential software consumers of the geometry and optimization, not covered procedures.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact full-class characterization is a finite-dimensional attained min--max functional, but evaluating correlated shifted Gaussian-cube probabilities and globally optimizing that generally nonconic objective can be computationally harder than solving the Bonferroni SOCP. The order-sharp family shows that the square-root spectral condition-number loss of fixed Bonferroni calibration cannot be removed uniformly, although particular covariance and donor geometries may yield a much smaller gap. The covariance remains known and prespecified; covariance estimation, selective donor choice, outcome-dependent weights, and transfer to a published estimator class are outside this version. The facial-reduction equivalence concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate faces and is not a general strict-\(W\) criterion. Its affine exposing multipliers, minimal face, and facial-dual bound are exactly certifiable, and its algebraic construction and verifier terminate, but no quantitative bit-complexity or practical-efficiency guarantee is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Finite-sample SOCP coverage, the exact full bounded-mean attainable-bias frontier, the covariance-domination sandwich, its square-root condition-number order-sharpness, weak nested-support dominance, and the rational strict witnesses are theorem-level results. The exact formula uses all existing \(L\) and \(\delta\) values and maximizes over the jointly attainable bias set; it does not assume simultaneous coordinatewise endpoint attainment. On the zero-bias class, \texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier} additionally gives a strict Loewner covariance criterion, while \texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier} gives the explicit product root. The exact finite certificate in \texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate} characterizes strict SOCP improvement on degenerate faces: its affine exposure identities are derived by an in-house separation lemma, and its real-algebraic construction and verifier terminate. It carries no quantitative runtime bound. Unknown covariance, covariance confidence sets, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, direct coverage claims for the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein estimator, and coverage claims for \texttt{scpi} or \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} are outside the paper. Correlated Gaussian-max numerical calibration is a post-solve refinement.
